name: Urban Priority Same-Day Couriers
author: urbanpriority

sections.description:
Urban Priority connects a WooCommerce store to the Urban Priority courier service. Shoppers at eligible addresses can select a delivery quote and pay the retailer at checkout. The retailer reviews the order and pays the separate courier fee through its Urban Priority business account. Once booked, shoppers can see tracking in their WooCommerce order when the store receives a tracking link.

Live pricing, merchant billing and dispatch require Urban Priority’s approval for the business and store. The plugin supports GBP checkouts with a single shipping package and a positive order total. The shopper pays through the official WooCommerce Stripe Payment Gateway. The store uses its checkout phone field so the courier can contact the recipient. Quotes depend on the collection and delivery postcodes, the approved service, booking time and courier availability. If a quote expires, refresh the checkout delivery options to request a new price.

On an approved test store, you can try delivery quotes, courier payments and bookings with test payment details. Test bookings do not request a driver.

External services

Urban Priority Ltd — accounts, quotes, bookings and tracking

  • Business application: when a store administrator submits the form, partner-api.urbanpriority.co.uk receives the company name, contact name, email, phone, store website, collection address and postcode, and the application consent and terms version.
  • Store connection: when the administrator approves or resumes setup, api.urbanpriority.co.uk receives the store URL, merchant and pairing identifiers, a read-only WooCommerce API key and secret, and a setup signing secret. The connected store exchanges signed verification messages with Urban Priority, including the store identity, approving WordPress user ID and approval time. These let Urban Priority verify control of the store, read eligible orders and deliver signed status updates.
  • Checkout quotes: when WooCommerce requests or refreshes a delivery price, including before checkout is completed, the store sends the checkout reference, service and vehicle, collection and delivery addresses and postcodes, available names, emails and phone numbers, and item names, SKUs, quantities and weights. Urban Priority uses these to check coverage, availability and price. Connected stores use api.urbanpriority.co.uk. Stores using a merchant API key send authenticated requests to partner-api.urbanpriority.co.uk or the approved test host below.
  • Retailer bookings: opening the business portal at portal.urbanpriority.co.uk sends the platform name and, where available, the merchant and selected order IDs. The connected store can supply a list of courier-selected orders with their IDs, dates, totals, payment and order status, recipient names, postcodes and chosen services. When the retailer reviews an eligible paid order, the service can also read its delivery and item details and captured-payment confirmation. The retailer reviews the separate courier charge in the portal. On status checks, the store sends the order reference to Urban Priority. Signed updates can return a booking reference, delivery status and tracking link to WooCommerce.
  • Shopper tracking: the order page and eligible order emails can include a link. Opening it sends the tracking token to the Urban Priority tracking service, along with ordinary browser request data such as the IP address. Rendering the link does not call that service. The plugin recognises older test links on courier-api-6gak.onrender.com locally and displays a verified legacy test link using partner-api.urbanpriority.co.uk.
  • Optional test and pilot connections: a paired LocalWP store sends signed test quote or status requests, including store identifiers and the corresponding quote details or order reference, to api.urbanpriority.co.uk. A separately enabled authorisation pilot uses connect.urbanpriority.co.uk for merchant identity. Only when enabled and used does it exchange the client and callback details, authorisation codes, verification values and tokens with that service.

Urban Priority platform terms | Urban Priority privacy policy

Render — hosting for Urban Priority’s test services

courier-partner-sandbox.onrender.com hosts Urban Priority's separate test API on Render. Only a store configured for that sandbox sends it the merchant's test API key, connector version and the quote or order details needed for the requested operation. Test booking, status, cancellation and reconciliation requests can include the order or quote reference. Opening a sandbox tracking link sends its tracking token and ordinary browser request data to that host. The older `courier-api-6gak.onrender.com` hostname described above is used for recognising saved test links.

Render terms of service | Render privacy policy

Stripe — shopper payment and capture verification

The official WooCommerce Stripe Payment Gateway sends the payment details needed to process the shopper’s payment to Stripe. When verifying an eligible order, the connector uses the store’s configured gateway to send the PaymentIntent and charge identifiers to Stripe’s API and to check capture, amount, currency, refunds and disputes. Urban Priority can obtain the resulting payment references and capture confirmation from the store when reviewing the order. The retailer’s courier payment is separate from the shopper’s checkout payment.

Stripe services agreement | Stripe privacy policy

Support

For coverage, account approval or a courier booking, contact Urban Priority.
sections.installation:
If you are upgrading from the private Urban Priority pilot, deactivate the pilot plugin before activating this release. Both versions use the same WooCommerce shipping method.

  1. Activate WooCommerce 7.0 or later and configure the official WooCommerce Stripe Payment Gateway. Set the store currency to GBP.
  2. Upload the plugin ZIP under Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, then activate it.
  3. On a public HTTPS store, open WooCommerce > UP Deliveries and follow the instructions to connect an Urban Priority business account. You can apply for an account from the same screen.
  4. Under WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping, add Urban Priority to the appropriate shipping zone. Enter the collection address, postcode and contact details, then select the approved services.
  5. After Urban Priority approves live pricing, billing, capacity and permissions, check the options at checkout using an address in the business’s delivery area and a contact phone number.
sections.changelog:
0.20.6

  • Sanitise the store-pairing security token, protect concurrent store and order operations, and clarify external service use.

0.20.5

  • Open the WooCommerce store in the business portal when setting up the connection or reviewing an order.

0.20.4

  • Offer same-day courier quotes at checkout, review and book deliveries in an Urban Priority business account, and show tracking on the shopper’s order.
